source.title_on_document: Exploration vs. Fixation: Scaffolding Divergent and Convergent Thinking for Human-AI Co-Creation with Generative Models

supplement.where: Appendices A-D, pp. 21-35 of this PDF; Appendix C.3, pp. 27-28; Table 4, p. 29; Table 5, p. 31; ablation prompts in Figs. 13-14, pp. 32-33.
supplement.holds: Technical implementation and validation (Appendices A-B); study environment, task instructions, interview protocol, participant demographics and counterbalancing (Appendix C.1); learning-response coding scheme (Appendix C.2); image pool, rater setup, rating rubrics and aggregation (Appendix C.3); system and ablation prompts (Appendix D). Appendix C.3 reports 123 downloaded posters from 24 participants: 63 with ChatGPT and 60 with HAICo (p. 27).

paper_design_summary: In a randomized within-subjects laboratory study, 24 local-university participants created poster images with HAICo and ChatGPT in counterbalanced task/system sequences (pp. 8-9, Section 5; p. 31, Table 5). Outputs were assessed for rated novelty and usefulness, downloaded-image fluency, within-participant CLIP image-set variety, and counts of distinct conceptual image clusters (p. 10, Section 5.3; pp. 11-12, Figs. 5c and 7). A separate model-only ablation reused the 24 initial HAICo prompts to compare associative and non-associative GPT-5 idea generation after the user study (p. 10, Section 5.3; p. 12, Fig. 7 right).

studies.label: Within-subjects lab study: HAICo vs ChatGPT (poster image creation)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Counterbalancing sequence (task pair, task order, and system order HAICo-first or ChatGPT-first); every participant used both systems
assignment.quote: This design resulted in 12 counterbalancing sequences (3 task pairs × 2 task orders × 2 system orders). Accordingly, we recruited 24 participants, with two participants randomly assigned to each sequence
assignment.locator: p. 9, Section 5 (continuing from p. 8); p. 31, Table 5

arms.name: HAICo
arms.description: Co-creation system with switchable Divergent mode (idea cards from associative-thinking prompting) and Convergent mode (structured refinement options); GPT-5 text and OpenAI image models

arms.name: ChatGPT
arms.description: Standard ChatGPT chat interface for image generation, same image model version

participants.exclusions: None for novelty, usefulness, and fluency. For the diversity measure, three participants who downloaded only one image for both systems were excluded, yielding N = 21 (p. 10).
participants.who: Members of the local technology-focused university recruited via mailing lists and word of mouth, aged 24 to 34, 21 of 24 from computer science or IT; the paper does not state their student or staff status
participants.country: not stated (participants received a 20 euro voucher; most authors are at German institutions)
participants.quote: We recruited 24 participants (10 female, 13 male, 1 non-binary) from the local university via mailing lists and word of mouth (aged 24–34 years, M = 28.2, SD = 2.8).
participants.locator: p. 9, Section 5.1; p. 29, Table 4 (Field of Study/Profession; student or staff status not identified)

ai_tool.name_model: HAICo (GPT-5 text; gpt-image-1, later gpt-image-1.5) vs ChatGPT (same image models)
ai_tool.how_used: Participants generated and refined poster images with each system; HAICo also supplied AI-generated idea cards in its Divergent mode

task.description: Create poster images promoting a behavior: Spend less time on phones, Spend more time outdoors, or Take care of your mind
task.duration: About 20 minutes of co-creation per session within a 40-minute session; study about 1 hour 50 minutes

outcomes.name: Novelty of downloaded posters
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Five raters (not authors; four had been study participants), blind to system, 5-point Likert; averaged across raters, then images per participant-system pair, then participants; ICC(2,5) = 0.61

contrasts.reported: HAICo M = 3.22 vs ChatGPT M = 2.41; W = 0.0, p < 0.001 (Wilcoxon signed-rank)

outcomes.name: Diversity of each participant's downloaded image set
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Average pairwise cosine distance between CLIP ViT-bigG-14 embeddings of one participant's downloaded images per system; variety within one person's outputs, not across people; N = 21 after excluding three participants with one image

contrasts.reported: HAICo M = 0.48 vs ChatGPT M = 0.36; W = 26.0, p = 0.001 (Wilcoxon signed-rank; N = 21)

outcomes.name: Usefulness of downloaded posters
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same five blind raters, 5-point Likert on how effectively the poster promotes the behavior; ICC(2,5) = 0.60 (p. 10, Section 5.3; pp. 27-28, Appendix C.3).

contrasts.reported: Usefulness was not significantly different across systems (numerical arm means, SDs, a test statistic, and an exact p-value are not printed).

outcomes.name: Fluency of downloaded posters
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of images downloaded per participant for each system; participants selected images they considered ready to print as posters (p. 10, Section 5.3, Downloaded Images; p. 27, Appendix C.3).

contrasts.reported: Fluency was not significantly different across systems. Numerical arm means, SDs, a test statistic, and an exact p-value are not printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 11, Fig. 5c and caption; p. 10, Section 5.3, Downloaded Images

outcomes.name: Image clusters (distinct conceptual ideas explored)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of distinct conceptual ideas represented by each participant's image clusters, derived from screen recordings. Each cluster comprises an initial image and its refinement variations; it counts conceptual variety within a participant rather than across people (p. 10, Section 5.3, Behavioral Metrics from Screen Recordings).

contrasts.reported: HAICo M = 2.88 vs ChatGPT M = 2.04; W = 33.0, p = 0.021 (Wilcoxon signed-rank). SDs are not printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 12, Fig. 7 left and caption; p. 10, Section 5.3, Behavioral Metrics from Screen Recordings; p. 9, Section 5.3 (test)

studies.label: Post-study model-only ablation: associative versus non-associative idea prompting

assignment.what_was_assigned: No human assignment: the same initial HAICo prompts from S1 were evaluated under both GPT-5 prompting conditions after the user study; generation order is not stated.
assignment.quote: After the study, using the 24 initial prompts participants entered into HAICo, we queried GPT-5 under both conditions three times each (9 ideas per run, matching HAICo’s configuration)
assignment.locator: p. 10, Section 5.3, Ablation: Associative-Thinking Prompting on Idea Diversity

arms.name: Associative-thinking prompting
arms.description: GPT-5 is instructed to generate ideas by drawing remote connections across domains; the Divergent-mode prompt is reproduced in Fig. 13 (p. 32).

arms.name: Non-associative-thinking prompting
arms.description: GPT-5 is instructed to generate creative and diverse ideas without the associative-thinking strategy; the comparison prompt is reproduced in Fig. 14 (p. 33).

participants.exclusions: No additional human sample; exclusions of input prompts are not stated.
participants.who: The 24 initial prompts entered into HAICo by S1 participants were reused as model inputs. These are matched prompt cases, not newly assigned or analyzed people.
participants.quote: After the study, using the 24 initial prompts participants entered into HAICo, we queried GPT-5 under both conditions three times each (9 ideas per run, matching HAICo’s configuration)
participants.locator: p. 10, Section 5.3, Ablation: Associative-Thinking Prompting on Idea Diversity

ai_tool.how_used: Researchers queried GPT-5 under both prompting conditions three times per initial prompt, generating 9 ideas per run; no people used the ablation outputs in a creative task (p. 10, Section 5.3).

task.description: Generate idea sets from the 24 initial HAICo prompts, comparing remote associative thinking with ordinary creative/diverse brainstorming; 9 ideas per run (p. 10, Section 5.3; pp. 32-33, Figs. 13-14).

outcomes.name: Within-set diversity of model-generated ideas
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Average pairwise cosine distance between CLIP ViT-bigG-14 encodings within each run of 9 model-generated ideas, averaged across three runs for each initial prompt and condition. n_units counts the 24 matched input-prompt cases, each evaluated under both conditions. This is model-only within-set variety, not diversity across different people (p. 10, Section 5.3). Figure error bars are bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals (p. 10, Section 6); numerical interval bounds are not printed.

contrasts.reported: Associative-thinking prompting produced greater idea diversity than non-associative-thinking prompting; W = 24.0, p < 0.001 (Wilcoxon signed-rank). Numerical arm means and SDs are not printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 12, Fig. 7 right and caption; p. 10, Section 5.3 (ablation methods) and Section 6 (figure uncertainty); p. 9, Section 5.3 (test)

company_involvement.description: Company involvement through authorship: Pronita Mehrotra is affiliated with MindAntix, USA, and Sumit Gulwani with Microsoft, USA. Company funding is not stated in the document.

eligibility.reason: S1 randomized participants to counterbalanced within-person task/system sequences and scored the resulting creative outputs (p. 9, Section 5; p. 31, Table 5; p. 10, Section 5.3). The same 24 people used both AI configurations, with 21 analyzed for image-set variety, below the 50-person threshold (pp. 9-10, Sections 5.1 and 5.3; p. 27, Appendix C.3). S2 is a model-only ablation reusing 24 initial prompts, not an additional human sample (p. 10, Section 5.3). The paper remains screening-report evidence: a small randomized experiment and a model-only study, with no eligible context class.

one_line_finding: With 24 participants in a within-subjects lab study, posters made with HAICo were rated more novel than posters made with ChatGPT (3.22 vs 2.41, W = 0.0, p < 0.001) and each participant's image set was more varied (CLIP distance 0.48 vs 0.36, p = 0.001, N = 21), with no significant difference in usefulness or fluency (p. 11, Fig. 5c).
notes: The complete markdown, including Appendices A-D, was read; recorded figures and correction evidence were checked against PDF pages. S2 measures variety within model-generated idea sets and is coded other/none because the codebook reserves diversity/across_people for comparisons across people. Appendix B technical checks concern latency, syntactic validity and execution fidelity rather than creativity outcomes; self-reported creativity support, usability and learning are also outside the output-scored outcomes.
